mainProgression.description: Driving power chord riff cycling between E5 and D5 with G5 providing a brief harmonic lift, all played at breakneck speed

sectionProgressions.description: Fast power chord progression driven by relentless downstroke picking at 164 BPM

harmonicFunction: E5 (i) - Tonic power chord establishing the dark minor key center
D5 (VII) - Subtonic creating the driving back-and-forth motion with the tonic
G5 (III) - Mediant providing a brief harmonic lift and contrast
The i-VII movement is the core engine of the song, creating relentless forward momentum
All chords are power chords (root + fifth) keeping the harmony ambiguously minor

techniques.name: Fast Downstroke Power Chord Riffing
techniques.description: The signature technique of the song - relentless downstroke picking on power chords at 164 BPM, requiring significant right-hand stamina and precision

notes: E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (Open low E string + 2nd fret A and D strings)
D5: X-5-7-X-X-X (5th fret A string + 7th fret D string) or 10-12-12-X-X-X
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (3rd fret low E string + 5th fret A and D strings)
All strokes are downstrokes for maximum attack and consistency
The fast tempo of 164 BPM makes this a serious right-hand endurance test
Slight palm muting adds tightness without killing sustain
sequence: Lock into the E5 power chord shape on the low strings
Drive consistent downstrokes with the wrist, not the arm
Shift quickly to D5 and back, minimizing hand movement
Hit the G5 on beat accents before returning to D5 and E5
tips: Build up speed gradually - start at 100 BPM and add 5 BPM per session
Relax your picking hand to avoid tension and fatigue at high speed
Use wrist motion rather than full arm movement for efficiency
Practice with a metronome to maintain absolutely steady timing
details.progression: E5 - D5 - G5 - D5 - E5 (Main Riff)

techniques.name: Palm Muting Rhythm
techniques.description: Controlled palm muting applied to the verse riff to add percussive tightness and definition to the fast power chord changes

notes: Rest the palm edge lightly on the strings near the bridge
Apply just enough pressure to dampen sustain without killing the note
Lift palm slightly on accented beats for dynamic contrast
Combine with downstrokes for the characteristic chugging sound
sequence: Position palm edge on bridge saddles
Play muted E5 power chord with steady downstrokes
Lift palm slightly for the chord changes to D5 and G5
Re-apply muting when returning to E5 riff sections
tips: The muting should be light - you still want pitch definition
Practice the palm muting separately from the chord changes first
Listen to the original to match the exact amount of muting Tony Iommi uses
Keep the muting consistent throughout the fast tempo
details.progression: E5 - D5 palm muted rhythm pattern

techniques.name: Pentatonic Lead Solo
techniques.description: The guitar solo uses E minor pentatonic patterns with blues-inflected bends and fast hammer-on/pull-off runs in the classic Tony Iommi style

notes: Based primarily in the 12th fret E minor pentatonic box position
Features whole-step and half-step bends on the B and G strings
Fast hammer-on/pull-off runs connecting pentatonic positions
Vibrato applied to sustained notes for expressive effect
sequence: Position in 12th fret E minor pentatonic box
Open with melodic phrases using bends on the B string (15th fret)
Add hammer-on/pull-off runs descending through the scale
Conclude with vibrato on a sustained bent note
tips: Learn the E minor pentatonic box at the 12th fret thoroughly
Practice bending to pitch with a tuner for accuracy
Keep the solo phrasing rhythmic and in time with the fast tempo
Iommi's style is melodic rather than shredding - focus on note choice
details.progression: E minor pentatonic over E5 - D5 - G5 - D5 - E5

sections.name: Intro/Main Riff
sections.description: The driving opening riff launches immediately into the fast E5-D5 power chord pattern that defines the song, establishing the relentless tempo from the very first note
notes: No introduction or buildup - the riff hits immediately
All downstrokes at 164 BPM from the first beat
Light palm muting on the E5 sections for definition
Sets the breakneck pace for the entire song

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse continues the main riff pattern with the same power chord progression, supporting the vocal melody while maintaining the driving momentum
notes: Same riff pattern as the intro continues without variation
Slight dynamic reduction to leave space for vocals
Maintain consistent palm muting throughout
The simplicity of the riff is its strength - do not embellish

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus simplifies to an E5-D5 alternation with slightly more open strumming, emphasizing the vocal hook
notes: Simplified two-chord pattern for the chorus
Slightly more open strumming than the verse
Accents align with the vocal melody for emphasis
Maintains the 164 BPM tempo throughout

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Tony Iommi's lead guitar solo over the verse progression, using E minor pentatonic licks with bends, vibrato, and fast pentatonic runs
sections.progression: E5 - D5 - G5 - D5 - E5 (repeating under solo)
notes: Solo primarily in the 12th fret E minor pentatonic position
Features signature Iommi bends and vibrato
Fast pentatonic runs that match the song's intense energy
Rhythm guitar maintains the main riff underneath

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The song ends with a return to the main riff, maintaining full intensity to the final abrupt ending
notes: Full return to the main riff at maximum intensity
No fade-out - the song ends decisively
Maintain energy and picking consistency to the final note
Clean cutoff on the final E5 power chord

guitar.pickup: Humbuckers, bridge pickup for maximum bite and attack

effects.distortion: Heavy amp gain is the primary distortion source - no pedals needed
effects.reverb: Minimal to none - keep it dry and tight
effects.other: No effects - pure guitar into overdriven amp for the raw Sabbath tone

beginner.title: Getting Started with Paranoid
steps: Learn the E5, D5, and G5 power chord shapes
Practice basic downstroke picking at slow tempo (80-100 BPM)
Work on transitioning between E5 and D5 cleanly
Build basic right-hand stamina with 2-minute downstroke exercises

intermediate.title: Building Speed and Stamina
steps: Increase downstroke speed gradually from 100 to 140 BPM
Add palm muting to the power chord riff
Learn the full song structure with all section transitions
Practice playing the complete song at 140+ BPM without breaks

advanced.title: Full Speed Mastery and Solo
steps: Play the full song at the original 164 BPM tempo
Learn the guitar solo with proper bending and phrasing
Develop endurance to play the entire song without hand fatigue
Match the original recording's tone and feel precisely

commonMistakes: Trying to play at full speed (164 BPM) before building proper technique
Tensing up the right hand, leading to fatigue and inconsistent timing
Neglecting palm muting, resulting in muddy power chord tone
Letting the tempo drift faster or slower during extended riff sections
Over-complicating the riff - the beauty is in its simplicity and relentlessness
practiceRoutine: Warm up with E5 downstrokes at 100 BPM for 5 minutes
Practice the E5-D5 change with a metronome, increasing 5 BPM per session
Work on the full three-chord riff pattern at a comfortable speed
Practice palm muting technique separately before combining with chord changes
Play along with the original recording once you can maintain 160+ BPM
focusAreas: Right-hand downstroke stamina and consistency at high tempo
Clean power chord shapes without buzzing or unwanted string noise
Precise palm muting control for tightness without killing tone
Smooth transitions between E5, D5, and G5 at full speed
Maintaining absolutely steady tempo through the entire song
metronomeWork: Start at 100 BPM with simple E5 downstrokes
Increase by 5 BPM per practice session once comfortable
At 130 BPM, add the D5 chord change to the pattern
At 150 BPM, add the G5 chord for the full riff
Target tempo is 164 BPM - do not sacrifice cleanliness for speed
